# Expected Merge

**Time Limit:** `1000 ms`  
**Memory Limit:** `256 MB`  
**Source:** [https://csacademy.com/contest/archive/task/expected-merge/](https://csacademy.com/contest/archive/task/expected-merge/)  

---

Consider the merge sort algorithm. It is usually implemented as a recursive function that sorts an interval. We divide the array in two halves, sort them recursively, and then merge the results.

If the interval being sorted has even length, the two halves will have equal size. But if the interval has odd length, then one of the halves will be greater than the other. In this problem we assume we choose uniformly and at random how to make the split.

Suppose we sort an array of size $N$. For each index $i$ we look at all the function calls that are done for an interval that contain $i$. If $S_i$ is the sum of lengths of these intervals, find the expected value of all $S_i$.

### Standard input

The first line contains a single integer $N$.

### Standard output

Print $N$ values representing the answer for each index $1 \leq i \leq N$.

### Constraints and notes

$1 \leq N \leq 10^5$ The result is checked with a precision of $10^{-6}$
